parsedVerdict.reasoning: PayrollService works like a domain/application service. It enforces business rules: only active employees can submit hours, and only approved timesheets are paid. It runs the approval workflow by calling sheet.approve() on the Timesheet entity, and it hands payslip calculation to Payslip.compute. Storage is reached only through repository calls (byId, create, approve, active, forWeek). The file contains no SQL, connection handling, HTTP, request/response handling or framework code. The weakest point is that the service builds domain entities from raw repository records itself (new Employee(...), new Timesheet(...), the `e.contract as Contract` cast, and spreading `{ ...sheet }` into create). Converting records into entities is arguably the persistence layer's job. Still, it is light glue code, not real persistence logic, so I don't count it as a layer-kind violation. Whether the service may depend on the concrete persistence classes is an import-direction question and out of scope.
